speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I need to understand the cause of your acute diarrhea. How long have you had these symptoms, and have there been any fever, blood in your stool, or recent travel?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection (C. diff). The history of recent levofloxacin therapy and the presentation of acute watery diarrhea with cramping are highly suggestive of an antibiotic-associated colitis. I will proceed with ordering a stool assay for C. difficile toxins.
